propositions: The bridge CLI provides a unified provider-neutral surface through canonical commands (setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) while retaining legacy reconcile and bridge-status compatibility.

Argument-less reconcile defaults to dry-run (non-mutating) while argument-less bridge sync defaults to live (mutating), with explicit compatibility adapters translating legacy exit codes 3/4/75 to canonical 0/1/2.

The same Python core bridge implementation is exposed through three interfaces (CLI, Python library, MCP server) across three install paths (brew, pip, MCP-server) without private reimplementations or editable checkouts.
Core operations remove GitHub gh CLI dependency and work identically across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments through shared command/secret/timeout contracts.
Python-owned tickets-branch delivery (src/rebar/_store/push.py) handles CAS retry, fetch-and-merge recovery, and push budget without workflow-local CAS loops.
Pause state is remotely persisted with reason metadata and safely readable by mixed-version fleets.
